mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in workplace attendance, indicated by WORKPLACES mobility remaining above -20% from baseline, signals a return of commuting routines that will gradually boost weekday retail footfall, producing higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If the average RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the average of the last 28 days, despite WORKPLACES remaining above -20% from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: Despite a recent dip, the high average level of parks mobility over the last two weeks suggests improving weather conditions or seasonal leisure activities are underway, which will spill over into increased general outdoor and leisure retail activity in the immediate future.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility is above 15% from baseline at t-0w and the average of the last two weeks is above 25%.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not increase in the following week despite PARKS meeting the specified trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decrease in residential mobility and an increase in workplace mobility indicates a shift away from home-centric activities, freeing up time and inclination for retail and recreation, driving an increase over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the last 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL decreasing and WORKPLACES increasing over the same period.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, a sustained recovery in transit station activity signifies increased public transport usage for commuting and leisure, directly supporting a rise in retail and recreation mobility over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains above -30% from baseline for two consecutive weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not show an upward trend over the next two weeks, despite TRANSIT remaining above -30% from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: The recent upward trend in RETAIL_REC from t-3w to t-1w, despite a minor dip in the last week, suggests underlying momentum towards recovery that will continue to push mobility higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean of the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained positive trend in grocery and pharmacy visits, indicating essential activities are normalizing, will free up consumer capacity and confidence for non-essential retail and recreation, leading to an increase over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above 0% from baseline for two consecutive weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next two weeks, despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining above 0% from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: High week-on-week volatility in parks mobility, coupled with RETAIL_REC being below -20%, suggests that good weather temporarily diverts people to parks, but this will rebound into increased retail and recreation as park activity normalizes, leading to a slight increase in RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS shows a week-on-week change of more than 20 points while RETAIL_REC is below -20% from baseline.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to decrease or remains flat in the next week, despite the described park mobility pattern.

mechanism_narrative: In a period of easing restrictions, a sustained decrease in residential mobility indicates people are spending less time at home, which directly translates to more opportunities for out-of-home activities including retail and recreation, driving an increase over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains below 7% from baseline for two consecutive weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the last 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL remaining below 7% from baseline.
